You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From 3c29b6038828c1f4c9ecbfec14d4fc5e25f1c947 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Christophe Leroy <christophe.leroy@c-s.fr>
Date: Fri, 10 Mar 2017 11:37:01 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] powerpc/8xx: fix mpc8xx_get_irq() return on no irq

IRQ 0 is a valid HW interrupt. So get_irq() shall return 0 when
there is no irq, instead of returning irq_linear_revmap(... ,0)

Fixes: f2a0bd3753dad ("[POWERPC] 8xx: powerpc port of core CPM PIC")
Signed-off-by: Christophe Leroy <christophe.leroy@c-s.fr>
Signed-off-by: Michael Ellerman <mpe@ellerman.id.au>
---
 arch/powerpc/sysdev/mpc8xx_pic.c | 2 +-
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/arch/powerpc/sysdev/mpc8xx_pic.c b/arch/powerpc/sysdev/mpc8xx_pic.c
index 3e828b20c21e..2842f9d63d21 100644
--- a/arch/powerpc/sysdev/mpc8xx_pic.c
+++ b/arch/powerpc/sysdev/mpc8xx_pic.c
@@ -79,7 +79,7 @@ unsigned int mpc8xx_get_irq(void)
 	irq = in_be32(&siu_reg->sc_sivec) >> 26;
 
 	if (irq == PIC_VEC_SPURRIOUS)
-		irq = 0;
+		return 0;
 
         return irq_linear_revmap(mpc8xx_pic_host, irq);
 
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by the incorrect handling of the return value in the `mpc8xx_get_irq()` function when there was no valid interrupt. Instead of returning 0 to indicate no interrupt, the function was returning the result of `irq_linear_revmap(..., 0)`, which is not appropriate since IRQ 0 is a valid hardware interrupt. This led to confusion and potential misinterpretation of the interrupt status. The patch corrects this by ensuring that the function returns 0 directly when there is no interrupt, aligning the behavior with the expected handling of IRQs.

Root cause:
The bug was caused by the incorrect handling of the return value in the `mpc8xx_get_irq()` function when there was no valid interrupt. Instead of returning 0 to indicate no interrupt, the function was returning the result of `irq_linear_revmap(..., 0)`, which is not appropriate since IRQ 0 is a valid hardware interrupt. This led to confusion and potential misinterpretation of the interrupt status. The patch corrects this by ensuring that the function returns 0 directly when there is no interrupt, aligning the behavior with the expected handling of IRQs.
